body:
Adds member alias templates to `basic_json` that create a `basic_json` type with one of its template parameters replaced, so you don't have to spell out all eleven:

```cpp
using my_json = nlohmann::json::with_string_t<my_string>;
// instead of
using my_json = nlohmann::basic_json<std::map, std::vector, my_string, bool, std::int64_t, std::uint64_t,
                                     double, std::allocator, nlohmann::adl_serializer, std::vector<std::uint8_t>>;
```

Aliases: `with_object_t`, `with_array_t`, `with_string_t`, `with_boolean_t`, `with_integers_t<I, U>`, `with_float_t`, `with_allocator_t`, `with_json_serializer_t`, `with_binary_t`, `with_base_class_t`. Together they cover all template parameters. They are members, so they also work from `ordered_json` or any other specialization and keep its other parameters.

This takes over #3898 by @barcode, which went stale. Their commit is included with them as author. On top of it, following the review in #3898:

- `with_changed_*_t` is renamed to the shorter `with_*_t`.
- The separate signed and unsigned integer aliases are merged into `with_integers_t<I, U>` (@gregmarr's suggestion), because the two are usually changed together.
- New documentation page `api/basic_json/with_t.md` with an example, linked from the `basic_json` index and `mkdocs.yml`.
- `std::is_same` tests for every alias in `unit-udt.cpp`, including one that checks `ordered_json::with_string_t` keeps `ordered_map`.
- Tests and examples that spelled out the full parameter list now use the aliases.

Supersedes #3898. Thanks @barcode!

## Public API

Only additions: ten new public member alias templates on `basic_json`. Nothing existing changes. No breaking changes.

comments.body:
Because this is a nested template type, these can chain.  This is not obvious and should probably be called out with an example.  Also, that it can start with `ordered_json` as well.

```
  using my_json = nlohmann::json::with_integers_t<int, unsigned int>::with_float_t<float>;
```

I did verify that  `nlohmann::json::with_object_t<nlohmann::ordered_map>` and `nlohmann::ordered_json` are the same type, as least as far as `typeid().name()` is concerned.  That's what I would expect.

Good point, thanks for checking. 8ab8fa934 adds a paragraph to `with_t.md` explaining that the aliases are members of every `basic_json` specialization (including `ordered_json`), so they can be chained:

```cpp
using my_json = nlohmann::json::with_integers_t<int, unsigned int>::with_float_t<float>;
```

It also notes that the order of chained aliases does not matter and that `json::with_object_t<nlohmann::ordered_map>` is `ordered_json`. These are now checked with `std::is_same` in `unit-udt.cpp` (both chaining orders, and `json` ↔ `ordered_json` in both directions).

*(Written by Claude Code.)*

@nlohmann Would you want to update the tests and examples to use this new functionality?  If so, would you prefer `nlohmann::basic_json::with_...` or `nlohmann::json::with_...` and would you want to change `...basic_json<my_object_type` to `...json::with_object_t<my_object_type>`.

In looking at this, I found a few places where only `integer_t` was changed, and a few places that all three numbers were changed.  There might be a case to have `with_integer_t` and `with_numbers_t` as well.

Thanks! Yes, done in #5787. It uses `nlohmann::json::with_…` (`basic_json` would need `<>`), and that includes the short `basic_json<my_object_type>` forms. I left out `with_numbers_t` / `with_integer_t` for now: the five int32/uint32/float sites read fine as `json::with_integers_t<std::int32_t, std::uint32_t>::with_float_t<float>`, and the signed-only ones as `with_integers_t<std::int32_t, std::uint64_t>`. If more call sites show up, we can still add a `with_numbers_t`.

*(Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.)*

>I left out with_numbers_t / with_integer_t for now

Sounds good.
